spins.label: Secretly Canadian
spins.publish_note: The War on Drugs is an American rock band from Philadelphia which was formed in 2005. The band consists of Adam Granduciel (vocals, guitar), David Hartley (bass guitar), Robbie Bennett (keyboards), Charlie Hall (drums), Jon Natchez (saxophone, keyboards), Anthony LaMarca (guitar), and Eliza Hardy Jones (percussion, keyboards). Founded by close collaborators Granduciel and Kurt Vile, the War on Drugs released their debut studio album, Wagonwheel Blues, in 2008. Vile departed shortly after its release to focus on his solo career, with Granduciel serving as the band's sole constant member thereafter. The band's second studio album Slave Ambient was released in 2011 to favorable reviews and a lengthy tour. The band's third album, Lost in the Dream, was released in 2014 following extensive touring and a period of loneliness and clinical depression for primary songwriter Granduciel. The album was released to widespread critical acclaim and increased exposure. Lost in the Dream is the third studio album by American indie rock band The War on Drugs, released on March 18, 2014, through Secretly Canadian. The recording session, which took place over a two-year period, was characterized by numerous rewrites. The album's lyrical themes were influenced by the loneliness and depression Granduciel faced after he finished touring. Musically, the record was inspired by 1980s rock, as well as Americana, with influences coming from Bruce Springsteen, Spacemen 3 and Neil Young & Crazy Horse.

spins.label: Solaris Recordings
spins.publish_note: Richard Mowatt, (born in 20 October 1972), commonly known by his stage name Solarstone (formerly spelled Solar Stone), is a British[2] trance DJ and producer based in Birmingham and Wales.[3][4] The music project Solarstone was founded in 1997 as a trio, and also used the pseudonyms Young Parisians, Liquid State and Z2. Over the years, Solarstone has developed a reputation for keeping to the original and classic trance sound. He is considered to be a veteran by fans in the trance music scene. Since 2012, Solarstone has been pushing forward a Pure Trance movement through tours where he aims to keep the trance genre true to its roots. The music project Solar Stone was founded in Dudley in 1997 by Richard Mowatt, Andy Bury and Sam Tierney. Since 1994, the trio had been known as the Space Kittens. Sam Tierney left the group in 1997 owing to musical differences, and in 2006 Andy Bury also left, leaving Mowatt as the sole member.

spins.label: Sister Jack
spins.publish_note: Collapse Under The Empire is a German instrumental post-rock duo from Hamburg. Founded in 2008, the group consists of Chris Burda and Martin Grimm. They have released nine studio albums and a number of EPs and singles. The band's fourth album, Shoulder & Giants, was released in 2011 and was the first part of a concept series, followed by Sacrifice & Isolation in 2014.[4][5] Shoulders & Giants received positive reviews. Visions magazine praised the "beyond all doubt, crystal clear production" and called it a "compelling and captivating album".[6] The music review website Plattentests.de highlighted the "imaginative arrangements" and "cinematic clouds of sound" and awarded it 8/10.

spins.label: Midium Records
spins.publish_note: Jakob is a New Zealand post-rock band, based in the Hawkes Bay city of Napier.[1] The band consists of guitarist Jeff Boyle, bassist Maurice Beckett, and drummer Jason Johnston.[1] They have been compared to such bands as Mogwai, Sonic Youth, and High Dependency Unit, though they largely eschew any vocals or samples in their songs. Subsets of Sets is the 2001 debut album by New Zealand post-rock band Jakob.

spins.label: Prophecy Productions
spins.publish_note: Unreqvited is an atmospheric/depressive post-black metal band from Canada, known for their unique sound that blends elements of blackgaze and post-rock. Band Background Unreqvited is a solo project created by the artist 鬼 (Ghost) from Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. Initially recognized for their blackgaze style, the band has evolved to incorporate a broader range of influences, moving away from traditional black metal to create a more personal and atmospheric sound. Music Style The band's music is characterized by a blend of lush post-rock elements and the intensity of black metal, often described as atmospheric and melancholic. Their latest album, "A Pathway to the Moon," showcases this evolution, reflecting the artist's personal influences and experiences.

spins.publish_note: Chicos de Nazca is a neo-psychedelic band from Santiago de Chile, based in Berlin, formed in 2010. South American psych rockers Chicos de Nazca and the band’s driving force, Francisco “KB” Cabala, formerly of the bands Cindy Sisters and La Hell Gang, have had quite an epic musical evolution. From their early days of playing their special recipe of South American psychedelia on the streets of Santiago on with a raw, young energy, complete with fuzzed up spaced out guitar and a healthy dose of wah, to their new home in Berlin, a recording studio, and a more refined sound. KB Cabala, the songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, and major force behind the band, talks about his recording studio, moving from Santiago to Berlin, and his new album teeming with love songs which, he tells us, has a “dreamy soul touch.”

spins.label: Grunt
spins.publish_note: Hot Tuna is an American blues rock band formed in 1969 by former Jefferson Airplane members Jorma Kaukonen (guitar/vocals) and Jack Casady (bass).[3] Although it has always been a fluid aggregation, with musicians coming and going over the years, the band's center has always been Kaukonen and Casady's ongoing collaboration. History 1969–1973: beginnings Hot Tuna began as a side project to Jefferson Airplane, intended to mark time while Grace Slick recovered from vocal cord nodule surgery that had left her unable to perform. They initially named the group Hot Shit but then decided on the more innocuous Hot Tuna.[4] That name came from someone Jorma Kaukonen referred to as a "witty wag" who called out "hot tuna" after hearing the line "What's that smell like fish, oh baby", from the song "Keep On Truckin' ".[5] Kaukonen, Jack Casady, Paul Kantner and new drummer Joey Covington played several shows around San Francisco, including the Airplane's original club, The Matrix, before Jefferson Airplane resumed performing to support Volunteers. (Although Covington had been hired by Jefferson Airplane, he only performed at select engagements, with Spencer Dryden continuing to perform as the band's principal drummer until his 1970 dismissal.)[6] Once the Airplane had resumed touring, Tuna found itself opening for the Airplane. Their early repertoire derived mainly from Kaukonen's Airplane material and covers of American country and blues artists such as Reverend Gary Davis, Jelly Roll Morton, Bo Carter and Blind Blake.

spins.label: Cleopatra
spins.publish_note: The Warlocks are an American rock band formed in Los Angeles, California, in 1998 by the guitarist/singer Bobby Hecksher. The band's music has ranged from psychedelic rock to drone music. There have been many changes in personnel since its formation, with Hecksher the only constant member. History The band was founded in 1998 in Los Angeles by Bobby Hecksher, adopting a name used by both the Velvet Underground and the Grateful Dead in their early days.[7] At the age of fifteen, Hecksher moved to Los Angeles from Florida with his family.[8] Hecksher's first instrument was cello, eventually moving on to bass guitar.[8] Hecksher's grandfather owned a radio station.

spins.publish_note: Wooden Shjips (pronounced "ships") is an American experimental and psychedelic rock band from San Francisco, California. History The project has released one EP and seven albums. Guitarist Ripley Johnson also plays in two side projects, including Moon Duo, formed in 2009 with Sanae Yamada. The group played at the 2010 All Tomorrow's Parties music festival in Monticello, New York in September 2010 at the request of film director Jim Jarmusch. Johnson has also released solo music under the name Rose City Band, including Sol y Sombra. They are signed to Thrill Jockey records. Musical style Their sound has been described as experimental, minimalist, drone rock, and "spacey psychedelic rock". They have been compared to Suicide, Spacemen 3, Loop, The Velvet Underground, The Doors, Soft Machine, Guru Guru, The Black Angels and many more. "Staring At The Sun" is a song by Wooden Shjips, released on May 25, 2018. The song is part of their album "V" and features a psychedelic sound with understated melodies. You can listen to it on platforms like YouTube or check out the lyrics on Genius. The song reflects themes of introspection and contemplation, capturing the essence of the band's artistic evolution.

spins.label: Wednesday Sound
spins.publish_note: Marcos Ortega, better known by his stage name Lorn, is an American electronic musician. Born in Normal, Illinois, Ortega grew up in central Illinois towns and eventually moved to Chicago, where he listened to electronic artists on the radio station WNUR as a teenager.[1] Since Lorn's first release in 2006 his music was played in the UK by Mary Anne Hobbs on BBC Radio and subsequently XFM, he has performed guest mixes several times for her radio shows.[2] Lorn was invited to create a track for the soundtrack of Darren Aronofsky's 2010 film Black Swan, which Mary Anne Hobbs was working on, however the track was not used.[2] Lorn signed with Flying Lotus' label Brainfeeder in 2009, and released his debut album Nothing Else in June 2010, which was mastered by electronic artist Clark.[3][4][5][6] He also received exposure in 2010 with his remix of grime musician Jammer's track "Better Than".[7] He lived in New York City for a time, and by 2010 had moved to Milwaukee, Wisconsin.[1] He released his second album, Ask The Dust (after the 1939 novel by John Fante), on Ninja Tune in 2012.[8][9][10] He produced an OST for the video game Killzone: Shadow Fall, which was released in 2014 also on Ninja Tune. Since 2014 he has released five albums, Vessel, A/D, REMNANT, RARITIES and DROWN THE TRAITOR WITHIN, as well as several EPs, on the independent label Wednesday Sound.

spins.label: Second Nature
spins.publish_note: secondnature presents a compilation of new music by our friends and peers in the Seattle electronic music scene. These tracks are fragmentary mirrors, reflecting moments we've shared on dance floors in Seattle clubs, basements, and warehouses. They are embers, conjuring the warm afterglow of rave memories that we are holding close in these strange times of isolation. Music connects us across time and space, rooting us in the past while pointing to the future. We all have to go our own ways for now, but the spirit of the rave endures

spins.label: Erased Tapes Records
spins.publish_note: Kiasmos is a Faroese-Icelandic minimal, experimental techno duo, composed of Ólafur Arnalds and Janus Rasmussen. They started in 2009 and released their first extended play, Thrown, in 2012 and their album Kiasmos in 2014. History In 2009, the duo started with the 65/Milo, a split 12"' release, together with record-label colleague Rival Consoles. In 2014, they released their debut LP, Kiasmos, on Erased Tapes Records Ltd.[1] Kiasmos released their fourth EP, Blurred, in 2017, which PopMatters described as "one of the most emotionally engaging electronic releases of the year . . . It is an intricate yet unforced and natural sounding set of songs with every song allowed room to bloom gradually."[2] Members Ólafur Arnalds and Janus Rasmussen worked together when Ólafur was a sound engineer for Rasmussen's Bloodgroup project.[3] Ólafur is a multi-instrumentalist and producer from Mosfellsbær, Iceland.[4] His work is characterized by strings and piano, with loops and edgy beats as a fusion of ambient/electronic and pop. Rasmussen, from the Faroe Islands, is a member of Bloodgroup. Rasmussen also worked along with other artists such as Guðrið Hansdóttir in the band Byrta.

spins.label: SecondNature
spins.publish_note: Seattle-based producer, DJ, and cofounder of the fantastic Apt E record label and party series, Cameron Kelley, aka tondiue We're beyond thrilled to welcome Seattle-based producer, DJ, and cofounder of the fantastic Apt E record label and party series, Cameron Kelley, aka tondiue to secondnature. As a spatial designer and bird watching hobbyist, they have a keen eye and ear for the meaningful details found within the natural world. This is expressed through their productions as well as DJ sets; often opting for the slow burning and meditative pace of percussive new age and textural ambient music, while bringing earthen timbres and frenetic rhythm to the dance floor. In addition to their explorations as tondiue, they make up one half of the DJ duo, party series, and record label Apt E alongside their longtime collaborator Max. Apt E has been making waves in the Seattle underground since 2017, starting with a series of all nighters at off-the-beaten-path locations around the city and later developing into a record label. Their vinyl releases focus on acts from in and around the Seattle area, and seek to provide a platform for up and coming artists. Look out for a handful of releases from tondiue in 2021, including an Apt E record from their newly formed krautrock band, Tape.

spins.label: Second Nature
spins.publish_note: Simic, also known as Ben Block, is an electronic music artist and DJ currently residing in New York, NY. He is a resident and event producer with secondnature, an electronic music collective based in Seattle, WA. Simic has a background in DJing and is known for his eclectic mix of techno and house music, often incorporating unique and playful sounds. The second release from Seattle-based collective secondnature comes from Simic with the Discussion of Interests EP. Three tracks of psychedelic and effective electronic music that falls somewhere between house and techno, along with a remix from Slow Life lead producer S. Moreira. Discussion of Interests is another marker in the development of secondnature’s musical realm, expanding it from the dark and cerebral techno of Fugal’s “Oil Panes” EP to one that includes more groove-laden tracks with expressive melodic content. SecondNature is an artist collective and label focused on bringing expansive electronic music to the Pacific NW.

spins.publish_note: Sandman Theory aka Nathaniel Blue creates Melodic Electronic Music. The Fuzzy Lounge Series is his Electronica, Trip-Hop side project. Conor Dean is a Seattle-based musician known for his unique blend of genres, including dub, trip-hop, blues, and downtempo electronica. His work is characterized by a heartfelt homage to the golden era of late-’90s electronica, with a focus on live instrumentation, analog synth textures, and vintage dub techniques. His album "The Fuzzy Lounge Sessions" is a testament to his artistic vision, featuring collaborations with local musicians and a full independent statement in music production. fuzzylounge.com Blending dub, trip-hop, blues, and downtempo electronica, The Fuzzy Lounge Sessions is the culmination of four years of studio work (2020–2024) at Sandman Theory’s Seattle studio, the Fuzzy Lounge. The album features collaborations with local musicians and fuses live instrumentation, analog synth textures, and vintage dub techniques—a heartfelt homage to the golden era of late-’90s electronica. The Fuzzy Lounge Sessions is not just an album—it’s a fully independent, artist-driven statement that bridges the tactile warmth of analog with the spacious depth of modern electronic production. Synthesizers and machines used: Roland Jupiter 6, TR-808, TR-8S, RE-150, Sequential Prophet 10 Rev3, Pro One, Access Virus TI2, Moog MiniMoog. The project was mastered by Grammy Award–winning engineer Reuben Cohen of Lurssen Mastering, with vinyl lacquers cut by legendary engineer Jeff Powell and pressing handled by Paramount Pressing & Plating (U.S.) on 180g black vinyl. The album will also be available in Dolby Atmos on Apple Music and Tidal for those wanting an immersive experience.

spins.label: Kscope
spins.publish_note: Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician. He is the founder, guitarist, lead vocalist, and songwriter of the rock band Porcupine Tree, as well as being a member of several other bands, including Blackfield, Storm Corrosion and No-Man. He is also a solo artist, having released eight solo albums since his solo debut Insurgentes in 2008. In a career spanning more than 30 years, Wilson has made music prolifically and earned critical acclaim.[4] His honours include six nominations for Grammy Awards: twice with Porcupine Tree, once with his collaborative band Storm Corrosion and three times as a solo artist. In 2017, The Daily Telegraph described him as "a resolutely independent artist" and "probably the most successful British artist you've never heard of".[5] Wilson is a self-taught composer, producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, and plays other instruments as needed, including bass guitar, autoharp, hammered dulcimer and flute. His influences and work have encompassed a diverse range of genres including pop, psychedelia, progressive rock and electronic, among others, shifting his musical direction through his albums. Wilson's fourth solo album, Hand. Cannot. Erase., was released on 27 February 2015. It was inspired by a documentary about Joyce Carol Vincent, a young British woman who lay dead in her apartment for nearly three years before being discovered.

spins.label: Triple Crown Records
spins.publish_note: Caspian is an American post-rock band from Beverly, Massachusetts, United States. History Early history: 2003–2004 Caspian loosely formed in Autumn of 2003 in Beverly, Massachusetts,[1] developing material through the first year of its existence, recording a demo in May 2004 and performing a small number of shows in late 2004 and early 2005, including support for the Japanese post-rock band Mono.[2] The band's first performance took place at The Pickled Onion in Beverly, Massachusetts on August 26, 2004. At the time, the band had not yet chosen the name Caspian and was looking for a vocalist. Waking Season is the third full-length studio album by Beverly, Massachusetts post-rock group Caspian. It is the group's first record to be produced by Matt Bayles and also their first to be released through Triple Crown Records. The album was released in CD, LP, 2XLP, and Digital Download formats on September 21, 2012 in Germany through Make My Day Records and worldwide on September 25, 2012 through Triple Crown Records.[6] An official music video for the opening track "Waking Season" debuted on Vimeo on September 25, 2012 and was directed by Daniel Navetta.[7] The album was later given an Australia / New Zealand release through Hobbledehoy Record Co in January 2014.[8] In an interview with Nothingbuthopeandpassion, guitarist Calvin Joss stated that the album is "anthemically about growth and change"

spins.publish_note: musicmaker. filmmaker. pacific northwest. Melodysheep, whose real name is John D. Boswell, is a Seattle-based musician and filmmaker known for his innovative approach to combining science and music. His work includes the "Symphony of Science" series, which blends electronic music with documentary film elements, and the "ORIGINS" series for National Geographic. Melodysheep has received multiple Webby Awards and is a TED guest, showcasing his impact on the creative community. His YouTube channel, melodysheep, has garnered over 431 million total views, and he has more than 3.1 million YouTube subscribers. Melodysheep's goal is to bring scientific knowledge and philosophy to the public through music, creating a novel way to engage with the world of science.
